subject.title: fix(opencode): public models work without configured credentials

question: Should OpenClaw officially support OpenCode Zen’s credentialless `public`-key mode for catalog models whose input-cost tiers are all zero?
rationale: The patch can implement the upstream client behavior, but deciding whether OpenClaw should expose this provider-auth mode and treat catalog cost metadata as its durable eligibility boundary is a product and compatibility decision.

options.title: Adopt the upstream contract
options.body: Merge after confirming that the OpenCode plugin may expose the documented model-cost-based anonymous mode and its upgrade behavior is acceptable.

options.title: Keep credentials mandatory
options.body: Decline the new mode and retain the current credential-gated OpenCode behavior until a broader provider-auth policy is defined.

options.title: Request a narrower explicit contract
options.body: Pause for an owner-defined allowlist or published provider guarantee if catalog cost metadata is not considered durable enough.

recommendation.title: Adopt the upstream contract
recommendation.body: Merge after confirming that the OpenCode plugin may expose the documented model-cost-based anonymous mode and its upgrade behavior is acceptable.

likelyOwner.reason: The contributor has the most directly documented understanding of the proposed OpenCode contract, while a long-term current-main area owner could not be established from the available review evidence.
